description:
Found by Fable`s s503 review probes of s501q (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s503/review/shadow2.pl` row e; `r503q-levers.pl` row 33).  PRE-EXISTING: base 2284d58d and the s501q tree answer the same, so perf round 38`s list-decl-split lever did not cause it (and did not fix it).

perl evaluates the right side of `my (LIST) = (LIST)` BEFORE the new variables exist, so `$q` and `$p` on the right are the OUTER ones.  PCL binds the new names first when the outer pair is LET-BOUND (declared in an enclosing block) and the inner declaration sits in an anon sub: both come out undef.

What works today (same file, perl == PCL): the single-scalar form `my $ox = $ox + 10` in an anon sub; the list form when the outers are FILE-level lexicals and the inner is in an anon sub, a named sub, a bare block or a loop body; one-element lists; a self-reference `my ($ox, $z) = ($ox + 1, 5)`.

What fails: shadow2.pl row e (outer in an enclosing BLOCK, inner in an anon sub inside it), and r503q-levers.pl row 33 (outers `my ($ox, $oy) = (1, 2);` at file level under `use strict; use feature q(signatures)`, inner inside an anon sub passed as an argument: `row "..." => sub { my ($ox, $oy) = ($oy, $ox); "$ox $oy" }` -- answers two empty strings where perl says `2 1`).  The two reproducers differ in how the outer pair is bound; minimise row 33 first (it is the file-level case that the smaller shadow2.pl rows b/c/d get RIGHT, so something else in that file -- the capture by other closures, the signatures feature, or the argument position -- is the trigger).

Sibling mechanism to grep first (rule 11): the single-decl shadow split in the variable-statement lowering (`my $i = $i + 1` parses the RHS before the rename) and s501q`s `list-decl-split` Kind-A lowering in Pl/Passes.pm, which already separates a literal list declaration into its declarations -- the same RHS-before-binding order is what this shape needs.

Bar: both reproducers + shadow2.pl all rows identical to perl; guard rows in the Pl/t file that holds the list-decl rows (perf-levers-07.t names the lever; pick a correctness file under the wall-time rule); scoping change => full sweep IS the gate, gate-SET scan over both populations.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a LIST declaration whose right side names same-named OUTER block-level lexicals reads the NEW (undef) variables -- `{ my ($p,$q) = (3,4); my $f = sub { my ($p,$q) = ($q,$p); "$p $q" } }` answers empty, perl `4 3`
